content:
My mom asked me why I suddenly decided not to start working right after graduation.I told her:

“Why not? I love the feeling of having options.I want to get into Big Tech—the money is great. But then again, maybe not—it’s exhausting, and I’d probably lose my hair to the grind. I want to be a Product Manager; the sense of achievement from building something is huge. But then again, maybe not—dealing with a hundred different personalities and playing the peacemaker sounds like a drag.

I want to make films, maybe join a top-tier production house like MediaStorm. I want to be a creator, like the guys at Speedster. I even want to build rockets from scratch in a backyard workshop.

I want to be a photographer, join a film crew, drive race cars for a factory team, or be a designer. I want to make music—play guitar in a dive bar and sing whatever song I’m obsessed with lately, not giving a damn whether the crowd is listening or not.

I just suddenly realized: if I finish a Master’s degree and just start climbing the corporate ladder, my life is basically set in stone. Sure, I’ll make plenty of money and settle down in a big city, but I’ll lose my choices. The cost of turning back will be too high. Kids need school, and a wife might be shouting about divorce every time she’s unhappy. Good God!

I just want to grab it all while I’m young: the best views, the best girls, the best version of myself, and the best opportunities.”

My Mom: 😮
title: The future is yet to come
